title: Sha'ban: the run-up
tomorrow: the whole Qur'an in one month. how does a family split it?

cards: Marathon plans don't start with the full distance; they start with weeks of shorter runs, and the race is half-won before the start line.

In a report in Sunan an-Nasa'i, Usama ibn Zayd notices the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ fasting a great deal in Sha'ban, and asks him why. His answer begins: it's a month people neglect, between Rajab and Ramadan.

teach.b: The rest of his answer: it's a month in which deeds are raised to the Lord of the worlds, and he loved for his deeds to be raised while he was fasting.

That's the same reason you met for Mondays and Thursdays, now stretched across a month. And Aisha, in Sahih al-Bukhari, says she never saw him fast more in any month than in Sha'ban, apart from Ramadan.
There's a twist at the finish line, too.

Another report in Bukhari says not to start fasting a day or two before Ramadan, unless it's a fast you already keep, like a Monday. The run-up builds, then it pauses at the line, so the big month starts fresh.

teach.h: MORE THAN ANY MONTH BUT ONE.
teach.b: So Sha'ban works as a run-up: shorter fasts, a little more reading, habits tried out before the big month arrives.
Here's the thing to tell a friend tonight: the quiet month between two well-known ones is the one he gave extra attention, because people forgot it.
Getting ready is part of the practice, not a delay before it.

how: In Sha'ban some Muslims add voluntary fasts, catch up on missed Ramadan days, and start reading more Qur'an, so that Ramadan's habits are already under way when the month begins.

games.q: your friend wants to fast every single day of Sha'ban to get ahead, and last year was worn out by the time Ramadan started. what fits?
o: a steady run-up: some fasts, some reading, no burning out.
nothing at all. save every bit of energy for Ramadan.
every day, no breaks. the harder the run-up, the better.
games.why: the Prophet filled Sha'ban with fasting as a run-up, and the white days showed steady beats heroic. the point is to arrive ready, not spent.

practice: Make a Ramadan plan in three lines. The wish: one thing you'd like that month to hold, a fast, a reading, a kindness. The obstacle: what usually gets in the way.
The plan: one small step you could start in Sha'ban, so the month doesn't arrive cold.

wordCard.voice: Sha'ban: the month before Ramadan, a run-up the Prophet filled with fasting, a month when deeds are raised.

orig.note: Arabic: Sha'ban, the month before Ramadan.

carryVoice: Remember it this way: getting ready is part of the month itself. Seven of fourteen, and Ramadan is next.
